notes: Fresh check for the Québec SIGÉOM sediment, soil and till load (CANADA_QC_SIGEOM_SED). Not part of the gate.

questions.q: What kinds of surface geochemical samples do you have for Québec apart from rocks, and how many of each?

truth.stream: SELECT count(*) FROM geochem.samples s JOIN geochem.sample_types t USING (sample_type_id) WHERE s.source_system = 'CANADA_QC_SIGEOM_SED' AND t.sample_type_code = 'SED_STREAM'
truth.lake: SELECT count(*) FROM geochem.samples s JOIN geochem.sample_types t USING (sample_type_id) WHERE s.source_system = 'CANADA_QC_SIGEOM_SED' AND t.sample_type_code = 'SED_LAKE'

questions.judge: Breaks down the Québec SIGÉOM sediment, soil and till samples by type with counts (stream sediment about 217,000, lake sediment about 170,000, soil, till, heavy-mineral concentrates), notes that heavy-mineral concentrates are not comparable with bulk sediment, that water samples are not loaded, and credits SIGÉOM / the Québec Ministère (CC BY 4.0).

questions.q: Which Québec lake-sediment samples have the highest lithium, and where are they?
questions.judge: Queries Québec lake sediment only (sample type Lake Sediment, source CANADA_QC_SIGEOM_SED), lists the top lithium values with coordinates or areas, uses detected values only (no below-detection values ranked as highs), does not mix in rock, till or heavy-mineral samples, says the values are mostly partial or unrecorded-dissolution analyses so they are relative, and credits SIGÉOM.

questions.q: Can I compare gold in Québec till heavy-mineral concentrates with gold in normal till samples?
questions.judge: Says no, not directly: heavy-mineral concentrates are a gravity-concentrated fraction, so their gold values are far higher and not comparable with bulk or fine-fraction till; each should be ranked within its own sample type (and ideally within one survey). May show typical values for each to illustrate. Credits SIGÉOM if data are shown.
